::: {#cor-ols-slope-r}
#### OLS slope in terms of the correlation

If $S_{xx} > 0$ and $S_{yy} > 0$, then

$$\hcoef{x} = r \, \frac{s_y}{s_x},$$

where $r$ is the
[Pearson correlation coefficient](exploratory-descriptive.qmd#def-pearson-r)
and $s_x$ and $s_y$ are the
[sample standard deviations](exploratory-descriptive.qmd#def-sample-sd)
of the $x_i$ and the $y_i$.
:::

::: proof

With the notation of @thm-ols-slr,
$r = S_{xy} / \sqrt{S_{xx} S_{yy}}$,
$s_x = \sqrt{S_{xx} / (n-1)}$, and $s_y = \sqrt{S_{yy} / (n-1)}$. So:

$$
\begin{aligned}
r \, \frac{s_y}{s_x}
&= \frac{S_{xy}}{\sqrt{S_{xx} S_{yy}}} \cdot
  \frac{\sqrt{S_{yy} / (n-1)}}{\sqrt{S_{xx} / (n-1)}}
&& \text{(substitute $r$, $s_x$, $s_y$)}\\
&= \frac{S_{xy}}{\sqrt{S_{xx}} \sqrt{S_{yy}}} \cdot
  \frac{\sqrt{S_{yy}}}{\sqrt{S_{xx}}}
&& \text{(cancel the factors of $n - 1$)}\\
&= \frac{S_{xy}}{S_{xx}}
&& \text{(cancel $\sqrt{S_{yy}}$)}\\
&= \hcoef{x}
&& \text{(closed-form OLS slope)}
\end{aligned}
$$

:::
